QF.id: Duplicate Share Certificates and Transmission of Securities_20

question.text: Kavita purchased shares off-market from Deepak, but the certificates were lost in transit before the transfer could be registered. What is the recommended course of action?

answer.text: Kavita should directly apply to the RTA for duplicate certificates in her name
Kavita should file an FIR and the transfer will be automatically processed
Kavita should ask Deepak (the holder) to apply for duplicate certificates and execute a fresh Form ISR-4
The stock exchange will issue replacement certificates to Kavita

explanation.text: The Logic: In an off-market transaction where the certificates are lost in transit, the workbook's prescribed course is that the claimant (Kavita) requests the security holder (Deepak) to apply for issuance of a duplicate share certificate and to execute a fresh Form ISR-4 to complete the off-market transfer. The Trap: The workbook also requires the claimant to provide an indemnity bond and an affidavit in support of the claim. The procedure is not a direct duplicate application by the buyer, nor is it triggered automatically by an FIR or by the stock exchange. Note: The off-market lost-in-transit procedure, including the request to the holder, the fresh Form ISR-4 and the claimant's indemnity bond and affidavit, is set out on pages 154-155 of the NISM-Series-II-A Registrars and Transfer Agents (Corporate) Certification Examination workbook (October 2025).
